events.subtitle: The Gilded Age: Part I
events.category: Chamber music / Gilded Age / Transatlantic cultural exchange
events.factual_description: Wolf Trap presents violinist Daniel Hope and pianist Maxim Lando at The Barns on Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 3:00 PM in The Gilded Age: Part I, the opening recital of a two-part series curated by Hope. The program is Enescu's Impromptu Concertante; Ravel's Violin Sonata No. 1 and the Blues movement from Violin Sonata No. 2; Elgar's Salut d'Amour and Chanson de Nuit; and Franck's Violin Sonata in A major. Wolf Trap frames the recital around the meeting of European musical refinement and American reinvention around the turn of the 20th century, with Hope and Lando providing moderated context during the performance.

en.why_it_matters: The draw is the argument of the program rather than rarity. Hope and Lando put violin and piano in a small room and move through a turn-of-the-century Europe already absorbing and reflecting new musical identities: Enescu's cosmopolitanism, Ravel's explicit Blues movement, Elgar's salon lyricism and Franck's long-form dialogue. As the first half of Hope's two-part Gilded Age idea at The Barns, it gives the later American-facing program a useful musical starting point instead of functioning as a generic recital.
en.trip_verdict: Worth keeping on the local calendar and attending if the afternoon fits cleanly. The Barns is an unusually good scale for this repertoire and the moderated concept adds context, but there is no need to displace a rarer premiere, farewell or one-off to make room for it.

es.why_it_matters: El atractivo está en la idea del programa, no en fingir rareza. Hope y Lando ponen violín y piano en una sala pequeña y recorren una Europa de cambio de siglo que ya estaba absorbiendo y reflejando identidades musicales nuevas: el cosmopolitismo de Enescu, el movimiento Blues de Ravel, el lirismo de salón de Elgar y el diálogo de largo aliento de Franck. Como primera mitad del díptico Gilded Age que Hope armó para The Barns, le da un punto de partida musical útil a la segunda parte más orientada hacia Estados Unidos en vez de funcionar como un recital genérico.
es.trip_verdict: Vale tenerlo en el calendario local e ir si la tarde embona bien. The Barns tiene una escala especialmente buena para este repertorio y la moderación añade contexto, pero no desplazaría por esto un estreno, una despedida o un one-off realmente más raro.
